+High specificity, medium readability. Custom orthogonal glyphs, ascender logic, full-bleed plate, and footer placement belong to this portfolio. At small widths it becomes a generic geometric texture instead of a readable signature.

+The deterministic detector found no component-level anti-patterns: `[]`, exit 0. Browser overlay scan found 21 page-wide findings, but those are not attributable to `SiteWordmark`: low contrast 4.2:1 ×14, low contrast 3.0:1 ×1, 10px Fig. 1 ×1, gradient text ×1, cramped padding ×1, line length ×4.
+
+## Overall impression
+
+Desktop feels authored. Mobile and dark static states feel unfinished. Biggest opportunity: decide whether this is a readable wordmark or atmospheric texture, then make that choice hold at every viewport and input mode.
+
+## What's working
+
+- Custom glyph geometry gives the footer a real signature.
+- Footer composition follows the site's stripe, hairline, rail, then full-bleed mark language.
+- Motion is restrained and reduced-motion aware.
+
+## Priority issues
+
+### [P1] Mobile wordmark collapses
+
+At 390px, the 1410×258 canvas scales to roughly 363×66px. The full handle compresses into a thin strip and no longer clearly reads `dhruv2mars`.
+
+Fix: use a mobile-specific mark such as `d2m`, or preserve a larger minimum glyph scale with a responsive alternate. Suggested command: `$impeccable adapt`.
+
+### [P1] Baseline contrast is too weak
+
+The outline uses `stroke-foreground/10`. Dark static mode nearly disappears; light mobile mode merges with the background. Pointer gradient carries too much legibility responsibility.
+
+Fix: raise baseline outline/fill contrast enough to read without hover. Keep gradient as enhancement. Suggested command: `$impeccable polish`.
+
+### [P1] Intentional clipping becomes accidental truncation
+
+`overflow-hidden` plus `translate-y-[25%]` removes about the lower quarter of the SVG at every viewport. Desktop can read this as a bleed; mobile loses the baseline and the mark looks cut off.
+
+Fix: reduce the bleed at small widths or change the crop so glyph bottoms remain identifiable. Suggested command: `$impeccable adapt`.
+
+### [P2] Numeral `2` is legible but optically inconsistent
+
+The new `2` is readable as a seven-segment block, but its full-width bars make it visually heavier than the surrounding letterforms. With the baseline clipped/faded, it becomes a dominant block instead of part of one word.
+
+Fix: redraw `2` using the same contour rhythm as the letters, then test it at 390px and in dark mode. Suggested command: `$impeccable polish`.
+
+### [P2] Interaction is pointer-only
+
+The gradient follows `onMouseMove` on a non-interactive div. Touch, reduced-motion, keyboard, and screen-reader users never receive the same legibility state. No cue explains the hover behavior.
+
+Fix: either make the mark genuinely decorative and remove interaction complexity, or expose a labelled, focusable interaction with a keyboard-equivalent state. Suggested command: `$impeccable harden`.
+
+### [P2] Footer social hit areas are 16px
+
+At 390px, X, GitHub, LinkedIn, and RSS anchors measure 16×16px. The project acceptance target is at least 24px, and 44px is safer for touch.
+
+Fix: keep 16px glyphs, expand hit boxes to at least 24px, preferably 32–44px on coarse pointers. Suggested command: `$impeccable harden`.

+
+Copyright/social content sits inside a 768px rail while the graphic spans the viewport. The mark can overpower the actual footer close and feel like a second hero.

## Specificity verdict

Custom and product-specific. Orthogonal glyphs, lowercase ascender logic, custom numeral, full-width plate all belong here.

But rendered result changes from “wordmark” to “faint geometric texture” on mobile and dark mode.

## What works

- Desktop footer feels like a deliberate signature.
- Graphic follows site language: stripe, hairline, rail, full-bleed mark.
- Motion stays restrained and supports reduced motion.

## Problems

### [P1] Mobile mark collapses

At 390px, full `dhruv2mars` compresses to roughly 363–374 × 66–68px. It no longer clearly reads as text.

Fix: mobile-specific `d2m`, or preserve larger glyph scale with an alternate composition.

### [P1] Contrast too weak

`stroke-foreground/10` makes static dark mode nearly disappear. Light mobile mode also blends into the background.

Fix: raise baseline contrast. Hover should enhance legibility, not rescue it.

### [P1] Bottom crop looks accidental

`overflow-hidden` + `translate-y-[25%]` removes about 25% of the SVG at every viewport. Desktop can read this as bleed. Mobile looks truncated.

Fix: reduce bleed on small screens or preserve glyph baselines.

### [P2] `2` reads, but does not fully belong

The new seven-segment `2` is recognizable. Its full-width bars are heavier than surrounding glyph contours. Combined with bottom clipping/fade, it becomes a dominant block inside the word.

Fix: redraw `2` using the same contour rhythm as the letters. Test at 390px and dark mode.

### [P2] Pointer-only interaction

Gradient follows `onMouseMove` on a non-interactive `<div>`. Touch, keyboard, reduced-motion, and screen-reader users never get equivalent feedback.

Fix: either make graphic truly decorative, or add labelled focusable interaction with keyboard state.

### [P2] Social hit targets too small

At 390px, X, GitHub, LinkedIn, RSS anchors are 16×16px. Project acceptance target is 24px minimum.

Fix: keep 16px icons, expand hit boxes to 24px minimum, preferably 32–44px for touch.

### [P3] Two competing endings

Copyright/social row sits inside a narrow rail. Graphic spans viewport. The mark can overpower the actual footer close and feel like a second hero.

Fix: choose one: readable brand mark or atmospheric texture. Tune scale/contrast around that choice.

## Persona red flags

- First-time visitor: mobile graphic does not clearly identify site.
- Mobile user: 16px social targets are easy to miss.
- Reduced-motion/touch user: misses the only state that boosts legibility.
- Dark-mode user: static wordmark looks nearly absent.

## Minor findings

- `aria-hidden` is fine if graphic remains decorative. Copyright text provides semantic fallback.
- Four social destinations are well grouped.
- No horizontal overflow at 390px, 768px, or 1440px.
- Desktop hover effect is tasteful but carries too much readability responsibility.
- Footer graphic sits close to fixed mobile dock, making final region feel crowded.
